detailed_description:
Angular stylised 3D animation, brush-stroke texture, Surrey, 1894, lit windows, black shadow.
[Shot 1] From 00:00 to 00:08. The shot opens on a medium close shot of <Subject 1> in the ochre tweed Inverness cape, black velvet smoking cap and steel spectacles on the brick steps of the observatory at night with the brass lantern raised in one hand, the broad ruddy face amused and sure, the full auburn beard, the plank door dark behind. The camera is on the gravel path level with his eyes, two long strides from him, a 50mm lens. The lantern comes from LOW at the RIGHT. At the first frame Ogilvy's head and shoulders fill the CENTRE of the frame from the TOP third to the ochre cape at the BOTTOM edge, his head a third of the frame's height, lit from LOW at the RIGHT. The plank door is dark at the LEFT edge and the starry sky is black across the TOP. The shot is inside this place: The garden knoll at Ottershaw on a warm starlit night in 1894: a small round observatory of white weatherboard on a red-brick plinth under a green copper dome with its slit open, a plank door with iron strap hinges, three brick steps, a gravel path. The camera pans right across the whole shot, travelling a finger's breadth as the plank door keeps the left edge, from 00:00 to 00:06. <Subject 1> (S1), on screen, broad ruddy face, with a clipped English voice at an even pace, says: <d>[English] The chances against anything manlike on Mars are a million to one.</d> His mouth shapes every syllable as the line is heard and closes on the last word. At 00:06, as the line ends, his free hand lifts and waves the thought away. At 00:07 the lantern swings a hand's breadth, and the swing continues to the last frame of the shot. By 00:08 the camera is panning right through the last frame, and the action continues with it.
